Off-peak departure prep rules
This page helps new colleagues see how a new handler works

This topic matters because off-peak prep is where small mistakes turn into delays, stress, or an unsafe handoff. At the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, your job is to keep the process calm, clear, and consistent. Start by checking the booking notes, the animal type, and the crate condition before you promise anything to the traveler. If the animal is small and the case looks wrong, stop and review it instead of guessing.

<<FACT F056>>

Use plain language with the traveler and stay steady if they seem rushed. If a pet like Maisie arrives with worn fittings, loose fasteners, or a blocked air opening, you do not push it through on goodwill. You inspect, correct, or escalate. That order matters. We want dependable companion travel, not last-minute heroics.

<<FACT F068>>

When the animal is a reptile, treat the crate check as a safety check, not a paperwork exercise. Weight, latch strength, ventilation, and secure footing all matter together. If anything feels off, do not improvise. Escalations follow a calm stepwise review, first to the senior coordinator and then to the next level if needed. Keep your tone even and your notes factual.

<<FACT F066>>

You may meet travelers who want a fast answer and a quick release. Slow the moment down. Confirm the booking details, match the animal to the approved crate, and verify that the crate is marked and ready for loading. If a traveler offers extra explanation, listen, but do not let side stories replace the checklist. Your standard is simple: check, confirm, and only then hand off.

Remember to stay calm, stay exact, and never let speed outrun the safety check.
